text: A fixed-width encoding assigns every symbol the same number of bits. Derive the width needed for some alphabets. Give each fill as a plain integer.
choices: 128 ASCII characters need exactly log2 128 = ___ bits
256 byte values need exactly log2 256 = ___ bits
Unicode's 1,114,112 code points need ceil(log2 1114112) = ___ bits
explanation: 5, 7, 8, and 21. The last is the interesting one: Unicode's space needs 21 bits, which fits in no natural machine word, and that awkwardness is why UTF-32 wastes 11 bits per character and why UTF-8 exists instead. Chapter 4 takes it up, and Chapter 33 shows that the waste in a fixed-width encoding can be quantified exactly.
